title: Coherent mates of squares along enhanced equivalences
statement:
Use the universes, enhanced categories, coherent functors and coherent natural equivalences of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $\mathscr A,\mathscr B,\mathscr A',\mathscr B'$ be enhanced categories. Specify adjoint equivalences $L:\mathscr A\rightleftarrows\mathscr B:R$ and $L':\mathscr A'\rightleftarrows\mathscr B':R'$, meaning coherent functors with units $\eta:\mathrm{id}\to RL$, $\eta':\mathrm{id}\to R'L'$ and counits $\epsilon:LR\to\mathrm{id}$, $\epsilon':L'R'\to\mathrm{id}$, all natural equivalences with specified coherent triangle identities. Let $V:\mathscr A\to\mathscr A'$ and $U:\mathscr B\to\mathscr B'$ be coherent functors and let $\alpha:L'V\simeq UL$ be a specified coherent natural equivalence. Composition below is written in the usual right-to-left order.

The composite
$$\theta_{U,V}:VR\xrightarrow{\eta'VR}R'L'VR\xrightarrow{R'\alpha R}R'ULR\xrightarrow{R'U\epsilon}R'U$$
is a coherent natural equivalence. The space of coherent transformations $\theta:VR\to R'U$ equipped with a homotopy
$$\epsilon'U\circ L'\theta\simeq U\epsilon\circ\alpha R$$
is contractible. Here the space means the homotopy fiber, over the specified right side, of postcomposition with $\epsilon'U$ after applying $L'$ to transformations in the enhanced functor categories. The displayed composite, with its mate homotopy from the triangle identities, is a point of that space.

For the identity square this mate is coherently the identity of $R$. Given a second such square $U':\mathscr B'\to\mathscr B''$, $V':\mathscr A'\to\mathscr A''$, $\alpha':L''V'\simeq U'L'$ and an adjoint equivalence $L''\dashv R''$, put $\alpha''=(U'\alpha)\circ(\alpha'V)$. Then the mate of the pasted square is coherently equivalent to
$$\theta_{U',V'}U\circ V'\theta_{U,V}:V'VR\longrightarrow R''U'U.$$
These comparisons are natural in coherent transformations of squares and satisfy all unit, associativity and higher pasting compatibilities for every finite composable string of squares. The vertical functors $U,V$ need not themselves be equivalences.
